$comment: SHARED City-State agent policy. This file is TRACKED and core-owned: edit it
in the core repository, then `git merge core/master` carries it to every
domain. Before this existed, the same policy was hand-copied into six repos,
which is the exact problem the core/domain split was built to remove.
Personal, machine-specific preferences (model, effort, thinking) belong in
.claude/settings.local.json, which stays untracked and overrides this file.

$comment_allow: Read-only inspection plus the write operations this project actually
performs. The previous allowlist covered only reads, so every real action
- add, commit, merge, push, gh, pytest - fell through to a prompt. That was
invisible because the app-level bypass was on; with bypass off, automation
would stall every few seconds. Anything not listed here still asks.
$comment_deny: Everything here is irreversible or breaks the core/domain architecture.
History rewriting is the critical addition. Every domain repository shares
an ancestor with core; rewriting core history breaks mergeability for all
of them at once, and no amount of care afterwards repairs it. The previous
list blocked `push --force` and `-f` but left --force-with-lease, rebase,
filter-branch, filter-repo, branch -D and update-ref -d wide open.
`git remote set-url` is denied because a domain silently repointed at
another repository is how a push lands in the wrong system. That very trap
was found live in the core folder on 2026-07-25.
Deny wins over allow, so the broad `git push` permission is safe: the
destructive forms below are still refused.
